learningObjective: Distinguish evidence-gated reactive pretraining from ad hoc recipe changes by tracing how a recoverable mainline checkpoint, controlled side probes, multiple diagnostics, and an explicit decision feed the next training phase.
mediumRationale: A deterministic vertical SVG is the smallest medium that can separate the expensive checkpointed mainline from low-cost experimental branches, then show evidence returning to a decision gate before the next phase. It makes observability and rollback structural prerequisites rather than items in a prose list.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected because the mechanism is a compact process graph, but this article benefits from precisely separating the persistent mainline, disposable side probes, evidence bundle, and rollback path within a narrow reading column without adding Mermaid runtime cost.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected because a fixed vertical layout can encode mainline continuity, branch-and-compare experiments, evidence aggregation, and the gated continue/change/rollback outcomes with established visual roles.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected because a checklist or table would name the safeguards but would not show that probes branch from the same checkpoint and must rejoin only through evidence.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected because choosing simulated probe outcomes adds controls and hidden states without improving the core operational distinction between reactive and arbitrary changes.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected because the Marin retrospective's timeline and experiment plots are not necessary for this learning objective. Although the Marin repository is Apache-2.0 licensed, the documentation images' complete third-party provenance was not independently established; no source image, data trace, wording, coordinates, or layout is copied.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected because the prose describes phases, observability, microannealing, and rollback separately, leaving readers to assemble the control loop that makes an unplanned training program scientifically defensible.

pages.insight: The preceding data-inspection checklist emphasizes inspecting samples, variation, labels, and model errors before choosing interventions, but does not connect those observations to a long-running checkpointed program.

The training-skeleton slide is the closest methodological match: it requires a trusted train/eval loop, explicit-hypothesis ablations, fixed controls, visualized losses and predictions, and interpretable metrics.
The adjacent sanity-check slide says to plot training and validation behavior, parameter-update ratios, activations, and gradients, closely matching the multi-signal observability prerequisite.

The next model-selection slide recommends changing one factor at a time, preserving seeds, and distrusting inherited schedule defaults, which supports controlled comparisons rather than untracked recipe drift.
The transformer slide introduces warmup and cooldown phases and notes that language-model loss follows scale, but presents a planned schedule rather than reactive decay-and-rewarm probes.
The neighboring instruction-tuning slide describes alignment tax and capability tradeoffs, relevant to Marin's SFT regression lesson but not the experimental control loop.
The next LLM slide emphasizes data preprocessing, distribution consistency, and later batch changes, but provides no checkpoint, side-probe, or rollback structure.
The LLM-data slide covers joint model/data scaling and mixtures of web and curated sources, motivating data-mix decisions without explaining how to test them during one continuing run.

deckReview.notes: All 214 pages of the local PDF were text-indexed page by page for pretraining, training data, data mix, perplexity, evaluation, checkpoint, learning-rate schedule, cooldown, fine-tuning, instruction, benchmark, ablation, and experiment terminology. Pages 58-61 were inspected as the complete closest training-method neighborhood; pages 102-106 were inspected around the deck's transformer schedule, instruction-tuning, and LLM-data treatments. Pages 162-165 discuss production experimentation and metrics but add governance breadth rather than the checkpointed reactive loop. No deck image, wording, data, coordinates, or composition is reused.

sourceReview.notes: The complete article's hardest mental model is the operational boundary between adaptive science and expensive improvisation. The original figure therefore does not reproduce Marin's phase timeline. It shows a generic phase checkpoint branching into a same-checkpoint control and candidate probe; per-domain loss, task evaluations, and parameter norms form the evidence bundle; an explicit gate chooses continue, change one factor, or restore the checkpoint; only then does the mainline advance. Named Marin examples annotate each role without asserting that every historical transition followed one identical protocol.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages and inspected the closest training-method and LLM-data neighborhoods, then checked the official Marin retrospective and repository, the WSD-S and OLMo 2 papers, the OPT logbook, and licensing guidance before selecting an original checkpoint-probe-decision loop.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG uses a linked title and detailed description, a solid vertical mainline, dashed disposable probe branches, direct labels for all diagnostics and outcomes, numbered stages, and a distinct rollback arrow. Meaning is carried by line style, position, text, and node shape rather than color. A single 360-unit viewBox with no minimum width scales in the established plot-panel primitive at 390 CSS pixels; existing theme variables preserve dark-mode contrast and shared print rules provide a light high-contrast rendering.
